section_summary: This section (pages 81–91) of State Department decimal file 894.0011 documents diplomatic exchanges and protocol concerning the Japanese Imperial Family between 1934 and 1935. It primarily details the official communications surrounding the birth and naming of Prince Akihito, including Emperor Hirohito's formal announcement, President Franklin D. Roosevelt's congratulatory reply transmitted via Ambassador Joseph C. Grew, and related State Department correspondence. The section also includes a 1934 cross-reference sheet concerning the visit of Prince Tsunenori and Princess Toshiko to Stockholm and an internal 1935 Far Eastern Affairs memorandum regarding diplomatic felicitations on imperial births.

subfiles.about: Emperor Hirohito informs President Roosevelt of the birth of his son, Prince Akihito, on December 23, 1933.
subfiles.summary: Hirohito's letter to Roosevelt announcing the December 23, 1933 birth of Prince Akihito and expressing friendship; concluding Japanese text dated February 5, 1934 with English translation.
subfiles.title: Letter from Emperor Hirohito to President Franklin D. Roosevelt Announcing the Birth of Prince Akihito, with Translation

subfiles.about: The Department of State instructs Ambassador Grew to deliver President Roosevelt's congratulatory letter to Emperor Hirohito and lodge an office copy with the Foreign Office.
subfiles.summary: Phillips sends Grew Roosevelt's March 28, 1934 autograph letter to Hirohito congratulating him on Prince Akihito's birth, with instructions for delivery and an office copy for the Foreign Office.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 508 from William Phillips to Joseph C. Grew, Transmitting President Roosevelt's Letter to Emperor Hirohito

subfiles.about: Acting Secretary Phillips informs the Japanese Ambassador that President Roosevelt has prepared an acknowledgment to Emperor Hirohito's announcement.
subfiles.summary: Phillips tells Ambassador Saito that Hirohito's announcement reached Roosevelt, whose acknowledgment was sent to Grew in Tokyo for delivery.
subfiles.title: Letter from William Phillips to Japanese Ambassador Hirosi Saito

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew reports the delivery of President Roosevelt's letter to the Japanese Foreign Office and encloses the diplomatic notes exchanged.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports he asked Foreign Minister Hirota on May 15, 1934 to convey Roosevelt's letter to the Emperor; Hirota replied May 18 that steps had been taken. Notes enclosed.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 799 from Joseph C. Grew to the Secretary of State, with Enclosures

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet noting Despatch No. 211 from Stockholm concerning the visit of Prince Tsunenori and Princess Toshiko to Sweden.
subfiles.summary: Document file note on Stockholm Despatch No. 211: Prince Tsunenori and Princess Toshiko arrived July 21; Prince Carl Jr. hosted them.
subfiles.title: Document File Note Regarding Visit of Prince Tsunenori and Princess Toshiko to Stockholm

subfiles.about: Far Eastern Affairs officers assess diplomatic protocol regarding felicitations upon the birth of an imperial child in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Far Eastern Affairs memorandum concluding no further action is needed on felicitations for an imperial birth, since Neville presumably acted under standing instructions, as with earlier princesses.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Division of Far Eastern Affairs Regarding Felicitations for Imperial Births
